tier_reason: Independent third-party comparison by the PCRE2-JIT author with public harness code (regex-test.tgz on zherczeg/sljit gh-pages: main.c, tre.c, pcre2.c, Makefile, MakeGlobals with CFLAGS -g -O3 -Wall), compiler stated (GCC 4.8.2 Linux, GCC 4.4.7 Windows). It falls short of A because the CPU is given only as 'Intel Xeon 2.67GHz' (no model; several Xeon generations share that clock), and the published tarball bundles PCRE2 10.20-RC1 (pcre2.h PCRE2_DATE 2015-06-16) while the page labels the baseline PCRE2 10.10, so the package does not exactly reproduce the labelled table.

corrections.baseline: PCRE2 interpreted pcre2_match, no JIT (page labels it PCRE2 10.10; the published harness tarball bundles PCRE2 10.20-RC1)
corrections.claimed_speedup: Mixed, not a project claim. x86-64 Linux, Intel Xeon 2.67GHz: TRE 0.8.0 beats interpreted PCRE2 on [a-zA-Z]+ing (954 ms vs 1373 ms, 1.44x, derived from page data) and .{0,2}(Tom|Sawyer|Huckleberry|Finn) (3425 ms vs 5164 ms, 1.51x, derived from page data) and ties on .{2,4}(Tom|Sawyer|Huckleberry|Finn) (5248 ms vs 5298 ms). x86-32 Linux run: 892 ms vs 1740 ms (1.95x), 3641 ms vs 6726 ms (1.85x), 5700 ms vs 7107 ms (1.25x), all derived from page data. x86-64 Windows, Intel Core i5 3.2GHz: 567 ms vs 773 ms (1.36x) and 2170 ms vs 2970 ms (1.37x), derived from page data, but slower on .{2,4}(...) (3298 ms vs 2965 ms). On the remaining 12 of 15 patterns (13 of 15 on Windows) TRE is slower than interpreted PCRE2, by up to 97x on Twain (486 ms vs 5 ms, derived from page data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: GCC 4.8.2 (Linux runs) / GCC 4.4.7 (Windows run). The page states only -O3; the harness MakeGlobals sets CFLAGS = -g -O3 -Wall, which the tre/ and pcre2/ sub-Makefiles include, so both engine libraries and the driver are built with -g -O3 -Wall. Bundled TRE 0.8.0 config: TRE_WCHAR and TRE_MULTIBYTE on, TRE_APPROX off; bundled PCRE2 10.20-RC1 with SUPPORT_UNICODE and SUPPORT_JIT. TRE called via tre_regcomp(REG_EXTENDED|REG_NEWLINE) and tre_regnexec; PCRE2 via pcre2_compile(PCRE2_MULTILINE, newline ANYCRLF) and pcre2_match.
corrections.workload: Find all non-overlapping matches of 15 regex patterns over the ~20 MB Mark Twain e-book mtent12.txt (carriage returns converted to newlines), restarting each search at the previous match end; best of 5 runs per engine, wall time in ms, engines built with default options. The HTML output prints only times, so match counts per engine are not shown on the page.
corrections.caveats: The evidence is a third-party comparison page by the author of the PCRE2 sljit JIT (Zoltan Herczeg, page last modified 2015-08-23), not a TRE claim, and TRE is not faster overall: it loses to interpreted PCRE2 on 12 of 15 patterns (up to 97x on Twain, 486 ms vs 5 ms), to PCRE2-JIT by up to 964x ([a-q][^u-z]{13}x, 1928 ms vs 2 ms) and to RE2 by up to 162x (Twain, 486 ms vs 3 ms), all derived from page data. Its wins come on patterns where the PCRE2 backtracker gets no start-of-match optimisation ([a-zA-Z]+ing, .{0,2}(alternation)); .{2,4}(alternation) is a 1 percent tie on x86-64 Linux and a loss on Windows. Against pcre2_dfa_match TRE wins 7 of 15 patterns on x86-64 Linux, but DFA mode is not the default. Versions are from 2015 (TRE 0.8.0; the page says PCRE2 10.10 while the published harness bundles PCRE2 10.20-RC1); current TRE and PCRE2 were not measured. Engines were not tuned (default options). PCRE2 uses leftmost-first Perl semantics and TRE leftmost-longest POSIX semantics, and the harness does not print match counts, so equal work per engine is not demonstrated. CPU is given only as 'Intel Xeon 2.67GHz' with no model number. Heng Li's regex benchmark (lh3lh3.users.sourceforge.net/reb.shtml) reportedly shows TRE third on alternation patterns but was not opened, so it is not used.

notes: All numbers in the record check out against the page (64-bit and 32-bit Linux tables), and metadata is correct (BSD-2-Clause per LICENSE, 925 stars, last commit 2026-05-23, not archived, not a fork). Shortcomings to record: not faster overall than PCRE2 (wins 2-3 of 15 patterns, loses by up to 97x), 2015-era versions with a 10.10 vs 10.20-RC1 label mismatch in the harness, CPU model not stated, match counts not shown. Evidence is valid (no reject grounds); no duplicate of a listed project found.
